previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for worsening right leg pain and ulcers, found to be due to calciphylaxis and severe peripheral arterial disease. She had markedly elevated PTH, leading to a parathyroidectomy, after which she developed hungry bone syndrome with symptomatic hypocalcemia requiring IV calcium replacement and close monitoring. A CT angiogram revealed critical stenosis in the right femoral artery, prompting angioplasty and stenting, complicated by distal embolization and persistent foot ischemia. Despite interventions, her right foot remained cool, dusky, and painful, with vascular surgery deferring amputation pending demarcation. Calciphylaxis lesions were managed with intralesional sodium thiosulfate after IV therapy was halted due to worsening hypocalcemia. Pain was controlled with a multimodal regimen, and anticoagulation was optimized for her mechanical valve. She was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing wound care, calcium monitoring, and outpatient follow-up with vascular and dermatology teams.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted after right below the knee amputation 
with Dr. ___ ___.  

Neuro: Preoperatively, she received a regional block by the 
acute pain service.  Postoperatively, she had significant RLE 
phantom pain that was poorly controlled and therefore the acute 
pain service started a ketamine drip and increased her dilaudid 
PCA. By ___, she was able to be weaned to pain medications by 
mouth, and by the time of discharge, she was no longer requiring 
any PRN doses of narcotics.  Of note, she did have chronic pain 
prior to admission and was requiring high doses of narcotics for 
pain control.  She will need to wean off of her oxycontin slowly 
post-discharge to avoid withdrawal symptoms. 

ID: Ms. ___ was started on vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and 
flagyl for cellulitis and she continued this treatment from 
___, as there was some erythema surrounding her right 
stump incision and small amount of necrosis. Her wound was 
monitored carefully and treated with daily dressing changes.

Heme/onc: Coumadin was held prior to her amputation and during 
the time period between the amputation and her second procedure, 
which was a left superficial femoral artery stent placement x 2, 
right common iliac angioplasty, and right groin angioseal by Dr. 
___ ___ for RLE peripheral vascular disease and 
symptomatic RLE ischemia.  In place of coumadin, she was 
maintained in a therapeutic range on a heparin drip for her 
mechanical aortic valve, which was placed in ___.  Coumadin 
was restarted ___ after her endovascular surgery and her INR 
was 1.4 on discharge, so she was sent on a heparin drip, which 
should be discontinued when her INR is in a therapeutic range, 
which for her is 2.5-3.5. 

FEN: The renal service followed Ms. ___ and provided 
hemodialysis and recommendations for electrolyte and fluid 
management.  Nutrition made recomendations for diet.

GI/GU:  Ms. ___ was kept on a bowel regimen while she was 
on high dose narcotics for pain control and she had regular 
bowel movements.  She had a foley catheter placed for the 
initial procedure, which was removed on POD 3 without incident.  


Ms. ___ is a ___ h/o ESRD on HD and CHF with prosthetic 
valve s/p R BKA, L SFA stents x 2 and R common iliac balloon 
angioplasty.  She was seen by physical therapy throughout her 
hospitalization and dilligently worked on her exercises 
independently.  She was discharged to an appropriate 
rehabilitation facility after verbalizing understanding of all 
discharge goals and plans.

Discharge Instructions:
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
DIVISION OF VASCULAR AND ENDOVASCULAR SURGERY
AMPUTATION DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS

ACTIVITY: 
On the side of your amputation you are non weight bearing for 
___ weeks. 
You should keep this amputation site elevated when ever 
possible. 
You may use the opposite foot for transfers and pivots.
No driving until cleared by your Surgeon.
No heavy lifting greater than 20 pounds for the next 3 weeks. 

BATHING/SHOWERING: 
You may shower when you get home
No tub baths or pools / do not soak your foot for 4 weeks from 
your date of surgery 
WOUND CARE:
Sutures / Staples may have been removed before discharge. If 
they are not, an appointment will be made for you to return for 
staple removal. 
When the sutures are removed the doctor may or may not place 
pieces of tape called steri-strips over the incision. These will 
stay on about a week and you may shower with them on. If these 
do not fall off after 10 days, you may peel them off with warm 
water and soap in the shower.
CAUTIONS:
If you smoke, please make every attempt to quit.  Your primary 
care physician can help with this.  Smoking causes narrowing of 
your blood vessels which in turn decreases circulation.  
DIET:
Low fat, low cholesterol / if you are diabetic  follow your 
dietary restrictions as before 
CALL THE OFFICE FOR: ___
Bleeding, redness of, or drainage from your foot wound
New pain, numbness or discoloration of the skin on the 
effected foot
Fever greater than 101 degrees, chills, increased redness, or 
pus draining from the incision site.
